title: A Warehouse Strike Became a Marketplace Liquidity Crisis
subtitle: Physical damage propagated through fulfilment, regional service, seller cash flow, employment, and the balance sheet of a state bank.

source.name: Wildberries operational, seller, employment, and debt reports summarized in input.txt

data.label: Logistics capacity hit
data.detail: More than half a million square metres of capacity were reported lost across nine days of attacks.

data.label: Regional service fails
data.detail: Belarus faced week-long delays, Crimea lost app coverage, and southern pick-up points stopped receiving goods.

data.label: Seller inventory is trapped
data.detail: Sellers could not freely recover goods or funds, while repayment credits were often only a fraction of lost value.

data.label: Local businesses lose cash flow
data.detail: Pick-up points and warehouse labour depended on continuous delivery volumes and were exposed to prolonged disruption.

data.label: State-bank exposure rises
data.detail: VTB holds a large direct exposure while also investing in Wildberries financial assets.

supportingFacts.label: Conservative warehouse reconstruction cost before equivalent or greater automation and equipment costs.
Total Wildberries debt reported by The Bell in the source text.

metadata.keyFinding: Physical warehouse damage propagated into regional service, seller liquidity, jobs, and bank exposure.
